title: Invertibility of the actual shifted Tate lines in all coefficient domains
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D, its coefficient datum C, a finite extension E of Q_l, a positive finite coefficient level n+1, a six-functor datum S on these coefficients, a finite-type D.k-scheme X, and integers m,t. Use the signed Tate objects of def-coefficient-twists-detailed and the actual closed domains of def-sf-datum. The literal reduction of the shifted integral Tate object O_E(m)[t] belongs to S.finiteTorDomain(X) and is tensor-invertible in (S.finiteClosed X).closed. The same integral object belongs to S.integralFiniteTorDomain(X) and is tensor-invertible in (S.integralClosed X).closed. The shifted rational Tate object E(m)[t] and the shifted common-stage Tate object Qbar_l(m)[t] are tensor-invertible in the rational and common closed domains, respectively; membership in both top domains is included. All shifts use their existing signed constraints. No internal-Hom comparison, evaluation naturality or exceptional inverse image is asserted.

source.place: final paragraph: each signed Tate line and each of its shifts is invertible

proof.text: Use the normalized opposite-line pair of lem-sf-perfect-dual-pair-and-tate-stability at m,t. Its representative equation identifies the underlying integral object with the shifted degree-zero complex of the signed rank-one completed Tate module; this is sfIntegralTwistingCoefficient(m)[t]. The rank-one module has Tor amplitude [0,0], and its shift has translated finite Tor amplitude. Thus this exact object belongs to the integral finite-Tor domain. The two normalized contractions exhibit its opposite signed shifted line as a tensor inverse, in the actual closed presentation. The faithful ringed-site realization reflects these isomorphisms. This includes m=0 and all negative m, and the Koszul shift signs are units for every integer t.

source.place: final paragraph: each signed Tate line and each of its shifts is invertible

proof.text: Apply the specified integral reduction to the integral representative. Its finite closed-model comparison identifies it with the signed finite Tate line shifted by t. Its rank-one finite representative has finite Tor amplitude, and the two opposite-line contractions are those of the normalized finite line pair. Therefore the literal reduced object in the statement belongs to finiteTorDomain and has a tensor inverse.

source.place: final paragraph: each signed Tate line and each of its shifts is invertible

proof.text: Rationalize the integral line and its opposite line. The normalized closed comparison carries the two contractions to contractions in the rational closed presentation. The shift comparison of rationalization identifies the image of the shifted integral line with sfRationalTwistingCoefficient(m)[t]. The rational domain is top, so this object belongs to it and is invertible.

source.place: final paragraph: each signed Tate line and each of its shifts is invertible

proof.text: Repeat the rational construction at the least finite coefficient field representing sfQbarTwistingCoefficient. The normalized commonClosedComparison transports both contractions to the common-stage category and commutes with the shift. Its literal representative formula identifies the result with the shifted sfQbarTwistingCoefficient in the statement. The common-stage domain is top. Opposite signed powers and opposite shifts provide the inverse. The local rank-one constructions also apply to the empty scheme.

source.place: final paragraph: each signed Tate line and each of its shifts is invertible

theorem sfShiftedCoefficientLinesInvertible
    {D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}} {C : D.CoefficientDatum} {E : Type u}
    [Field E] [Algebra (Padic C.l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic C.l) E] {n : ℕ}
    (S : SixFunctorDatum D C E (n + 1) (Nat.succ_le_succ (Nat.zero_le n)))
    (X : SixFunctorSpace D) (m t : ℤ) :
    (∃ hL : S.toSixFunctorOperationDatum.finiteTorDomain X
        ((sixFunctorIntegralReduction D C E n X).obj
          ((@sfIntegralTwistingCoefficient C.l _ E _ _ _ X.obj.left
            (dlAdicGeometricResidueInvertible D C X.obj.left) m)⟦t⟧)),
      @IsInvertible _ _ (S.finiteClosed X).closed.monoidal ⟨_, hL⟩) ∧
    (∃ hL : S.toSixFunctorOperationDatum.integralFiniteTorDomain X
        ((@sfIntegralTwistingCoefficient C.l _ E _ _ _ X.obj.left
          (dlAdicGeometricResidueInvertible D C X.obj.left) m)⟦t⟧),
      @IsInvertible _ _ (S.integralClosed X).closed.monoidal ⟨_, hL⟩) ∧
    (∃ hL : (⊤ : ObjectProperty (sfRationalConstructibleCategory C.l E X.obj.left))
        ((@sfRationalTwistingCoefficient C.l _ E _ _ _ X.obj.left
          (dlAdicGeometricResidueInvertible D C X.obj.left) m)⟦t⟧),
      @IsInvertible _ _ (S.rationalClosed X).closed.monoidal ⟨_, hL⟩) ∧
    (∃ hL : (⊤ : ObjectProperty
        (generalAlgebraicallyClosedConstructibleCategory C.l C.Qbar X.obj.left))
        ((@sfQbarTwistingCoefficient C.l _ X.obj.left
          (dlAdicGeometricResidueInvertible D C X.obj.left) C.Qbar _ _ _ m)⟦t⟧),
      @IsInvertible _ _ (S.commonClosed X).closed.monoidal ⟨_, hL⟩)
